title: Cloud Computing
topics: Cloud in AI and Big Data

bullets.text: Overview of cloud computing's meaning, importance, features, models, advantages, challenges, and applications.
Aim to provide a clear understanding of cloud computing's role in the digital world.
Delivery of computing services (servers, storage, databases, software, AI) over the internet.
Access computing resources on demand from providers instead of owning physical hardware.
Analogy: paying for electricity consumption without owning the power plant.
Makes technology more affordable, scalable, and convenient.
On-demand self-service: users access resources without human interaction.
Broad network access: services available over the internet from various devices.
Resource pooling: providers share resources across multiple customers securely.
Rapid elasticity: resources scale up or down quickly based on demand.
Measured service: usage is monitored and billed according to resources consumed.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): delivers fundamental computing resources like virtual machines, storage, networking (e.g., AWS EC2).
Platform as a Service (PaaS): delivers infrastructure plus a development platform with built-in tools (e.g., Google App Engine).
Software as a Service (SaaS): delivers ready-to-use applications over the internet, accessed via a browser (e.g., Gmail, Microsoft 365, Zoom).
Public cloud: shared by multiple organizations over the internet; cost-effective but with potential security concerns.
Private cloud: dedicated to a single organization, offering more control and security but higher cost.
Hybrid cloud: combines public and private clouds for a balance of flexibility and security.
Community cloud: shared by several organizations with common goals or requirements (e.g., healthcare).
Reduces costs by eliminating heavy investment in hardware and maintenance.
Improves scalability, allowing businesses to easily expand or reduce resources.
Enhances flexibility, enabling access to applications and data from anywhere.
Provides reliability through backup, disaster recovery, and high availability.
Supports innovation by allowing faster experimentation and deployment.
Security and privacy concerns regarding sensitive data stored on remote servers.
Downtime risk due to dependence on internet connectivity.
Compliance with strict regulations in certain industries (e.g., healthcare, finance).
Vendor lock-in, making it difficult and costly to switch providers.
Performance concerns for applications requiring high processing speed or low latency.
Real-world applications include data storage (Google Drive), business collaboration (Slack), entertainment (Netflix), healthcare, education, and research.
Cloud computing supports AI and Big Data analytics by providing on-demand high-performance computing resources.
Edge computing processes data closer to the source for reduced latency, relying on the cloud for storage and management.
Future trends include multi-cloud strategies, serverless computing, enhanced security, and integration with AI, blockchain, and 5G.
